bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory compliance and product stewardship across multiple global regulators — BRSR flags non-compliance with applicable regulatory requirements such as the US FDA, EMA, MHRA and WHO, and strict US/EU product-packaging rules, as risks that 'can lead to expensive product recalls and reputational damage'. The manufacturing review records that seven units received EIRs from the US FDA during the year, and consumer/customer complaints numbered 4,056 filed in FY26 with 752 pending resolution at year-end (4,593 filed and 641 pending in FY25) - so inspection outcomes and complaint volumes are a live watch-item for a company whose entire turnover is regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing.
- Geographic and channel concentration in the US and Europe, with US revenue exposed to transient product sales — The US and Europe together accounted for 73% of total revenue in FY26. The US formulations business was down 3% y-o-y, 'primarily impacted by lower transient product sales' - a reminder that a material part of US revenue is opportunistic rather than base business. Industry commentary in the same section notes intensifying loss-of-exclusivity dynamics (impact expected to rise to USD 179 billion from USD 49 billion in the prior five years) and increasing scrutiny over drug pricing and reimbursement policies in the US.
- API pricing pressure, competitive intensity and geopolitical risk in emerging markets — API segment revenue declined 6% y-o-y in FY26, with the Company stating business sales moderated 'due to pricing pressure in the antibiotics portfolio, intense competition and geopolitical risks in select emerging markets'. The outlook explicitly describes the API business as 'dynamic, shaped by pricing pressure, competitive intensity and geopolitical uncertainties'. Margin protection currently depends on the mix shift towards non-antibiotics.
- Dependence on institutional ARV procurement, with PEPFAR funding expected to moderate — The ARV business is anchored in institutional channels including PEPFAR, the Global Fund and the Government of South Africa. Management states 'PEPFAR support is expected to moderate gradually over the coming years', shifting the procurement landscape towards the Global Fund and local government funding, which 'could also increase the relevance of local manufacturing and packaging capabilities in select markets' - a structural change in how this segment's demand is sourced.
- Antimicrobial resistance and antibiotic manufacturing effluent — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications: improper management of antibiotic waste during manufacturing can release APIs into the environment, contaminating aquatic ecosystems and fuelling AMR, and the Company concedes that 'effective and scalable solutions to manage this risk are still being sought'. Mitigation is membership of the AMR Industry Alliance. This is structurally material given the scale of the beta-lactam / antibiotics portfolio.
- Climate transition and energy cost/regulation exposure — BRSR identifies Climate Change as a Risk with negative implications: stricter climate regulations, renewable energy mandates and emissions reduction targets impose transition risk requiring higher compliance costs, operational changes and significant investment in low-carbon technology, while extreme weather events can disrupt supply chains, cause resource scarcity and inflate raw material costs. Energy Management is separately flagged for rising energy costs, stringent regulatory savings targets and the fossil-to-renewables transition.
- Supply chain sustainability, human-rights compliance and new disclosure regimes — Sustainable Supply Chain is flagged as both risk and opportunity: climate disruption raising raw material and logistics costs; legal penalties from instances of forced labour, child labour or excessive working hours in the chain; and stricter global regulation such as India's BRSR Core and the EU's CSDDD 'demanding extensive supply chain-related disclosures' that require significant investment in process set-up and reporting systems. Awareness training on the Supplier Code of Conduct has so far reached suppliers accounting for 77% of key starting material (API) suppliers.
- Talent attraction/retention and occupational health & safety across a 40,000-strong workforce — Workforce Wellbeing is flagged for a dynamic and highly competitive job market, with limited growth opportunities or skill mismatches leading to disengagement, increased attrition and productivity loss; the Company employed 27,000+ permanent and 13,000+ contractual employees as of March 31, 2026. Occupational Health and Safety is a separate Risk with negative implications - 'gaps in adherence to safety protocols, lack of real-time monitoring, or insufficient training risk recurring safety failures, leading to enforcement actions and reputational damage'.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Aurobindo develops, manufactures and commercialises high-quality, affordable medicines worldwide, spanning generic formulations, specialty products and active pharmaceutical ingredients across regulated and growth markets. Its finished-dosage portfolio covers oral solids, liquids, injectables, OTC, derma and biosimilars across CNS, cardiovascular, antibiotics, ARV, anti-diabetics, gastroenterology, oncology and dermatology, sold to generic customers, major pharma customers, institutional customers and healthcare professionals. The API business supports both captive requirements (53% of APIs captively consumed) and external customers including innovators and large generic companies, and the group is building future-ready platforms in biosimilars and biologics contract manufacturing.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Shift the portfolio towards high-barrier, complex therapies: Eugia's development is centred on oncology, complex injectables, antibiotics, GLP-1 products, peptides, depot injections, ophthalmic suspensions, monobactams, niche cephalosporins, long-acting penicillins and PrEP anti-retrovirals for LMICs, prioritising products where scientific complexity, market relevance and manufacturing depth create long-term value.
- Build a global biosimilars franchise through CuraTeQ Biologics, combining in-house development and manufacturing with a commercialisation footprint across the EU and emerging markets plus selective entry into the US, with the longer-term aim of becoming a significant biosimilars player by 2030.
- Concentrate biosimilar development in oncology and immunology with disciplined resource allocation to priority programmes and a lean clinical development approach that draws on Phase 3 waivers where regulators permit.
- Scale a full-service, globally competitive biologics platform via TheraNym Biologics, Aurobindo's dedicated biologics contract manufacturing organisation, anchored by the MSD relationship.
- Deepen backward integration and manufacturing integration - the Pen-G and 6-APA facilities achieved operational stability during FY26, reinforcing backward integration initiatives and supply chain reliability, with continued ramp-up across newly commercialised plants.
- Strengthen the sterile injectables backbone through the Eugia Steriles Vizag injectable facility, adding qualified manufacturing lines and a dedicated peptide line.
- Advance complex injectable platforms including device-based injectables, long-acting injectables, suspension-based depot injectables and polymeric-based technologies, with depot injections a key area of focus.
- Expand differentiated drug-delivery platforms - dermatology topicals and transdermal patches, and respiratory nasal sprays and MDI/DPI inhalers manufactured at the Raleigh, USA facility - including a partnership with a global pharmaceutical company to develop complex respiratory products for acute and chronic conditions.
- Grow Europe market share through new launches and sustained momentum, operating in ten EU/UK countries across pharmacy, hospital and tender channels where the Company ranks among the top 10 generic companies in 8 countries.
- Strengthen Growth Markets presence through new product launches, market share expansion and entry into new geographies, including ramping up the Taizhou (China) facility which received EU GMP and Chinese GMP and commenced supplies to the European market.
- Sustain ARV leadership by leveraging supplementary business opportunities, efficient capacity utilisation, operational optimisation and new/supplementary contract awards, anchored in Dolutegravir-based regimens.
- Direct R&D across 6 centres and 1,500+ scientists towards biosimilars, generic APIs and generic formulations including orals, injectables and complex products such as inhalers, nasal sprays, depot injections and transdermal patches, with a focus on Specialty Drug Delivery Systems (SDDS).
- The routed governance text states no dividend-distribution, payout, buyback, debt-reduction or reinvestment PHILOSOPHY. The only capital-allocation content present is the 39th AGM ordinary resolution placing the interim dividend declared by the Board for the financial year 2025-26 for members' confirmation and approval, and the general governance philosophy that 'the corporate objective is to maximize shareholder value ethically and legally' and that the Company 'will continue to strive to be a wealth creator to meet stakeholders expectations'.
- Occupational health and safety: obtaining ISO 45001:2018 certification for the plants, with safety committees in place and prioritised OH&S training for employees and contractors.
- Climate/energy transition actions: transitioning to renewable energy and substituting coal with biomass, upgrading to energy-efficient technologies and conducting energy audits.
- Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) assessments carried out on key products to reduce the environmental impact of products and align with customers' carbon reduction goals.
- Waste and materials: co-processing of hazardous waste and packaging optimisation to reduce plastic waste, in response to tightening rules such as EU Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging waste.
- Antimicrobial resistance: membership of the AMR Industry Alliance, committed to increasing access to high-quality antimicrobial products, encouraging responsible usage and reducing environmental concerns.
- Responsible sourcing: a Supplier Code of Conduct is in place, local sourcing is prioritised as a key business objective, and supplier evaluation assesses credibility, environmental procedures, manufacturing techniques and commitment to environmentally friendly practices; the Supplier Code of Conduct has been communicated with awareness training to 77% of key starting material (API) suppliers.
- Water management is identified as an ESG opportunity centred on water reuse and recycling (the disclosure is truncated in the supplied text).
- Human capital and social programmes: a learning and development ecosystem, employee engagement initiatives (Chai Pe Charcha, Auro Josh, Leadership Talk Series), the structured Saksham child development programme and safety-linked rewards; Inclusion, Diversity and Equality is treated as a positive-implication material issue.
- Governance and grievance architecture: Policy on Business Ethics and Values, Human Rights Policy, Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy, Whistle Blower Policy, Supplier Code of Conduct and Investor Grievance Redressal Policy, plus a public adverse-event reporting channel for consumers; CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Enterprise risk governance: an ERM framework based on the COSO ERM Framework 2017 with a dedicated enterprise-risk department, and a Risk Management Committee (Mr. Girish Paman Vanvari as Chairman, Mr. Santanu Mukherjee and Dr. M. Madan Mohan Reddy) whose Risk Management Policy explicitly covers sustainability/ESG, information and cyber-security risks and a business continuity plan.
- Corporate Governance is identified as an ESG opportunity through alignment with evolving disclosure mandates such as the EU CSRD and SEBI regulations.
- No quantified ESG target (for example a net-zero or emissions-reduction year, a renewable-energy share, or a water-positive goal) is stated anywhere in the supplied text - only the qualitative initiatives listed above.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Aurobindo operates 32 modern manufacturing and packaging facilities across several countries (28 in India and one each in the USA, China, Portugal and Brazil) plus 6 R&D centres spread across 16,000 sq.m, and states it is continuously expanding led by backward integration into key starting materials (KSMs) and intermediates. Backward integration across Pen-G, 6-APA and Amoxicillin is described as strengthening supply security, reducing import dependency and improving the long-term margin profile; the Pen-G facility was successfully commercialised and stabilised during FY26, and based on current operating levels management expects annualised Pen-G production to exceed 10,000 metric tonnes with capacity utilisation levels exceeding 80% at consistent yields. In biologics, the Company launched TheraNym, its biologics CMO platform; commissioning activities for TheraNym Unit 1, a 60 kL integrated mammalian cell culture facility, are progressing as planned and are expected to be fully completed by the end of 2026, and the Company is separately expanding both bulk drug substance manufacturing and fill-finish capacities to support future growth and long-term manufacturing-readiness. In China, the OSD facility - which currently has a manufacturing capacity of 2 billion dosages - continues to scale up on the back of increasing product approvals and growing supplies into international markets, particularly Europe. The stated way-forward actions are to progress commercialisation and scale-up of the Dayton and Raleigh (USA) facilities with incremental capacities across oral, respiratory and transdermal product segments; to complete GMP certification for the Vizag facility and further strengthen it through the addition of cartridge filling lines, prefilled syringes (PFS) and BFS infrastructure; and to continue evaluating debottlenecking and brownfield expansion opportunities to enhance manufacturing flexibility, optimise asset utilisation and support long-term growth. Multiple capacity enhancement initiatives were advanced across manufacturing facilities during FY26 to support rising global demand. Geographic expansion is being pursued through new subsidiaries in Malaysia and the Philippines and entry into Algeria, Morocco, Egypt, Francophone West Africa, Ghana and Nigeria, adding to an operating footprint that already includes subsidiaries in South Africa, the UAE, Thailand and Saudi Arabia and greenfield operations in Tanzania and Kenya. Inorganic expansion comprises the ongoing Lannett acquisition in the US (to be completed and integrated subject to necessary regulatory approvals) and recent India acquisitions, while in Europe the Company remains focused on evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and expansion into new geographies. Analytical method transfers to Ace Laboratories in the UK de-bottlenecked testing at the Malta facility. The Chairman's/MD's strategic-priority KPI panel states 'Capex investments ~ ` 3,000+ crore' for FY26; this figure is presented as a KPI bullet and not as a labelled capex disclosure, so it is recorded here in narrative only and is not carried into capex_disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global pharmaceutical industry grew 9.3% in 2025 to an estimated USD 1,939 billion from USD 1,774 billion in 2024, driven by rising chronic disease incidence, an ageing population, higher R&D investment, advances in biologics and biosimilars, personalised medicine and digital health.
- The global pharmaceutical market is estimated at USD 2.6 trillion by 2030, growing at a 5-8% CAGR (2026-2030), led by new products and patent expiries including the growing impact of biosimilars; usage is projected to reach 4 trillion defined daily doses by 2030.
- GLP-1 receptor agonist market estimated at USD 71 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 202 billion by 2033 at a 13% CAGR, driven by rising obesity/diabetes prevalence, new launches and combination therapies.
- Global oncology drugs market estimated at USD 242 billion in 2025, projected to grow from USD 267 billion in 2026 to USD 667 billion by 2034 at a 12% CAGR.
- Global immunology market of nearly USD 180 billion in 2024 growing at 4-7% CAGR to USD 234 billion by 2029, with growth moderated by biosimilar erosion as blockbuster brands lose exclusivity up to 2030.
- Loss-of-exclusivity wave is a direct opportunity: palbociclib, enzalutamide and olaparib all lose exclusivity in 2027, and PD-1 inhibitors pembrolizumab and nivolumab are expected to face biosimilar competition starting 2028.
- Global biologics CMO market estimated by industry at approximately USD 22 billion in 2025, growing to over USD 40 billion by 2030 at a 12-15% CAGR - the addressable market for TheraNym.
- Rising demand for antibacterials alongside the need to manage antimicrobial resistance, and growth in neurology/mental-health treatment markets, support the antibiotic and CNS portfolios.
- FY26 saw stable performance across businesses and markets supported by sustained demand, operational resilience and continued execution of strategic priorities; Europe crossed the EUR 1 billion revenue mark.
- Margin lever from the Taizhou facility commencing European supplies after receiving EU GMP and Chinese GMP, described as supporting margin improvement with a steady ramp-up in operations.
- Continued price erosion in certain ARV products, offset by efficient capacity utilisation, operational optimisation and award of new and supplementary contracts.
- Macro backdrop: global growth of 3.3% in 2025 expected to remain steady in 2026-27 with global inflation cooling to 3.8% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027; Indian GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in FY2025-26 with FY2026-27 real GDP projected between 6.8% and 7.2%; India-EU FTA concluded in Q4 FY2025-26 and an interim India-US bilateral trade deal signed.
- 888 cumulative ANDAs filed in the US as on March 31, 2026 with estimated total market potential of US$192 billion per IQVIA; 728 final approvals, 35 tentative approvals and 125 under review (160 ANDAs in different stages of review).
- During FY26 the Company filed 29 ANDAs with the US FDA including 4 for specialty products, and received final approvals for 37 products including 3 specialty products; 42 products launched in FY26.
- Eugia FY26: 54 global submissions across major markets (around 30 oncology-focused), 8 US ANDA filings, 31 approvals received and 38 launches across major markets.
- Eugia FY27 plan: 80+ global submissions planned and 30+ submission batches planned for regulated and semi-regulated markets; key planned submissions include Pen-G, Tirzepatide, Aztreonam, Cetrorelix, Lenacapavir and Avibactam + Ceftazidime; key planned launches include Nintedanib, Isosulphan Blue and Cyclosporine.
- First long-acting depot product, Paliperidone Palmitate, filed with the US FDA; four peptide products in advanced stages of development.
- Injectable specialty pipeline of 181 ANDA filings, including 144 approved products and 37 pending approvals; 195 injectable products in the portfolio including those under development.
- CuraTeQ pipeline of 14 biosimilar candidates at year-end, concentrated in oncology and immunology; approved/filed assets include Dazublys (trastuzumab), Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim), Zefylti (filgrastim) and Bevqolva (bevacizumab); BP16 (denosumab) and BP11 (omalizumab) completed Phase 3.
- Dermatology portfolio of 58 topical products and 12 transdermal patches including those under development; respiratory portfolio of 16 nasal spray products including those under development.
- Canada portfolio expanded to 220 approved products with 62 additional products awaiting final approval at the end of FY26; China had 18 product approvals up to March 31, 2026 with manufacturing planned across facilities in India.
- 1,100+ ARV dossiers filed globally (Company-wide).
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Revenue growth was driven by Europe and ARV despite Revlimid phase-out, while EBITDA margin held at 20.4% ex-Revlimid; key catalysts include Pen-G ramp-up, biosimilar launches in Q3-Q4, and Lannett integration, all supporting margin expansion and cash flow strength.

open.item: Indonesia operations to continue at ~USD 8 million per quarter for the year, with efforts to ramp up further.
Elevated R&D spend (Phase-3 clinical trials for 4 biosimilars) expected to continue for at least another 4 quarters before filings.
Trastuzumab (CDSCO approved) to be sold via co-marketing partners for the first two quarters, with an in-house domestic biosimilars sales team kicking in by end of CY2025.
Pomalidomide (generic Pomalyst) to be launched this quarter as a first-to-market launch, already prepared.
Eugia-III recent USFDA inspection observations are procedural/technical (no data integrity issues, no production stoppage); company to respond within 15 working days.

OSD China facility (advancing toward 2 billion units annual capacity; EU approval for 10 products, 3 local approvals) expected to achieve EBITDA break-even in Q4 FY26 and meaningfully contribute to bottom-line EBITDA next year.
Pen-G facility expected to produce more than 10,000 metric tonnes on an annualized basis over the next 12 months, ramping to ~65-70% by March 2026 (vs last-year average of 42%).
On trajectory to exceed €1 billion in annual European revenue by the close of FY26.
Confident of achieving internal EBITDA margin target of mostly the higher side of 20-21% for FY26.
Europe to cross the milestone of €1 billion in annual revenues for the region by the end of FY26.
gRevlimid settlement quantities largely exhausted (limited sales next 1-2 quarters); company prepared to take more market share when the market opens up from 1 February 2026.
Confident of achieving internal target EBITDA margin of 20-21% for FY26.
Europe margins, previously mid-teens, now moving strongly above high teens and touching the 20% mark very soon.
Phase-1 of new GLP-1 API facility expected ready by end of next year (~100 kg capacity), expandable to another 400 kg in Phases 2-3.
Eugia-3 classified OAI; ~20+ of 29 pending ANDAs expected to be stuck, with at least 1 year of impact and a hoped-for return in the second year.
Expect ~USD 30-40 million of new product revenue in FY25-26 from balance of Eugia plants (50% from Eugia III, 50% from other plants), with growth mainly from gRevlimid.
Eugia's lead peptide product is targeted for submission in early FY27, with three additional peptide products planned for execution through Eugia Steriles' dedicated peptide line.
open.promised: early FY27 submission of lead peptide date

open.item: Lannett acquisition (FTC process, no negative surprises on overlap) expected to close early in the next fiscal year, in Q1 FY27.
Dayton US facility has transitioned to commercial phase and will begin contributing revenues significantly from FY27 onwards; Raleigh remains on track pending regulatory clearance.
Full margin benefit of Pen-G/6-APA (aided by the one-year MIP) expected to show from April 2026 onwards, once low-priced market stock is consumed and 6-APA predatory pricing corrects.
